title: spec review: R16 v2: orchestrator/stale.py — complete stale-work evidence (interface via raw graph links, tests, dependency, graph, overlapping merge) with pinned risk reasons and one source of truth for the worktree (AP P12)
spec:
Why: daemon.stale_check (orchestrator/daemon.py:1050-1070) compares only moved paths against scope plus changed files and grades none/low/high; brief P7 also requires interface, relevant-test, dependency, graph-relationship and overlapping-merge signals with base, goal head, relevant paths, risk, action and conflict outcome. v2 after spec review T-0576: interference.load_graph drops the link relation, merged tasks carry no changed_files, and a separate worktree kwarg would be a second source of truth.
What: new pure module orchestrator/stale.py; daemon delegation is a later task, so today's stale_check keys stay a subset of the output.
- load_links(root=ROOT) -> {"files": {node_id: source_file}, "links": [{"source", "target", "relation"}]} read directly from graphify-out/graph.json (nodes[].id/source_file, links[].source/target/relation); None when absent or malformed. Freshness via interference.graph_fresh_for(files, graph) where graph is interference.load_graph(root) for the same files.
- evidence(task, *, goal_ref=None, graph_links=None, graph=None, tasks=None, git=None) -> {"base": task_ref, "goal_head", "moved_count", "stale_paths", "signals": {"scoped_files_changed", "changed_files_moved", "tests_changed", "interface_changed": [{"symbol", "file", "consumer"}], "graph_relationships": [{"source_file", "target_file"}], "dependency_changed": [ids], "overlapping_merge": [ids]}, "risk": none|low|medium|high|unknown, "risk_reasons": [...], "graph": used|absent|stale|skipped}. Worktree comes only from task["worktree"] (like daemon.stale_check); every git call receives cwd=task["worktree"] through the injectable git callable (signature git(*args, cwd) -> CompletedProcess), and gitutil.moved_paths / gitutil.changed_paths are called with that same callable.
- Signals: moved = gitutil.moved_paths(task_ref, goal_ref); changed = gitutil.changed_paths(task); scoped_files_changed = moved matching scope patterns; changed_files_moved = moved ∩ changed; tests_changed = moved paths equal to tests/test_<stem>.py for stems of changed or scoped orchestrator/*.py; interface_changed = nodes defined in a moved file with a link of any relation to a node defined in a changed or scoped task file, when graph_links is given and the graph is fresh for those files (else graph = absent|stale and the signal is skipped); graph_relationships = distinct (moved file, task file) pairs behind those links; dependency_changed = depends_on ids whose merged sha (task record "sha") is not an ancestor of task_ref (git merge-base --is-ancestor); overlapping_merge = execute tasks in `tasks` merged into goal_ref whose scope literals or, when present, task["changed_files"] intersect the task's changed or scope paths and whose sha is not an ancestor of task_ref (changed_files is optional and populated by a later merge task; scope-literal matching is the floor).
- Risk and pinned reasons: high with reasons among "changed_files_moved", "interface_changed", "dependency_changed"; medium with "tests_changed", "graph_relationships", "overlapping_merge"; low with "scoped_files_changed"; none with []; unknown with ["git_failed"] on gitutil.GitError. risk_reasons lists every signal that fired, in that order.
- row(task, evidence, action, conflict=None) -> dict for schedlog.append("stale", ...) with task, goal_id, base, goal_head, changed_relevant_paths, risk, risk_reasons, action (recorded|rebased|rebase_conflict|revalidated), conflict paths. Never mutates git; never discards work.
acceptance: tests/test_stale.py::test_interface_change_in_moved_file_consumed_by_task_is_high_risk — graph_links with a link from a symbol in a moved file to a node in the task's changed file yields interface_changed non-empty, risk high and risk_reasons containing interface_changed
tests/test_stale.py::test_relevant_test_change_is_medium_risk — tests/test_foo.py moved while the task changed orchestrator/foo.py yields tests_changed, risk medium, risk_reasons ['tests_changed']

tests/test_stale.py::test_dependency_merged_after_branch_point_is_high_risk — a depends_on task whose sha is not an ancestor of the task ref (git callable answers merge-base --is-ancestor with rc 1) yields dependency_changed and risk high

tests/test_stale.py::test_overlapping_earlier_merge_uses_scope_literals_and_optional_changed_files — a merged execute task whose scope literal matches appears in overlapping_merge; one matching only through its changed_files list also appears; risk medium

tests/test_stale.py::test_absent_or_stale_graph_falls_back_and_git_failure_is_unknown — graph_links None yields graph absent with deterministic signals intact; a stale graph yields graph stale and no interface signal; a git callable raising GitError yields risk unknown and risk_reasons ['git_failed']; row() carries base, goal_head, changed_relevant_paths, risk, risk_reasons, action

risks.issue: Spec mandates a single injectable git callable shaped `git(*args, cwd) -> CompletedProcess` and says gitutil.moved_paths/gitutil.changed_paths 'are called with that same callable.' But those functions invoke their own `git` param positionally as `git(cwd, *command_args)` (see gitutil.py: `git(cwd, "merge-base", base_ref, target_ref)` and `git(worktree, "diff", ...)`), matching `_git_in(worktree, *args)`'s convention, not `git(*args, cwd)`. Passing the spec'd callable straight through will raise TypeError on every real call (cwd lands in *args, keyword-only cwd is left unbound); gitutil wraps generic Exception into GitError, so moved_paths/changed_paths will unconditionally fail whenever the mandated callable shape is used. That drives risk to 'unknown' for essentially every task and breaks all acceptance tests except the explicit git_failed case, which is the opposite of what those tests assert.

Freshness is specified as `interference.graph_fresh_for(files, graph)` with no git/cwd override. graph_fresh_for's default runner derives its cwd from `graph["path"]` (graphify-out/graph.json's grandparent, i.e. repo ROOT), not from `task["worktree"]`, and diffs `built_at_commit..HEAD` there. Every other git call in this spec is pinned to cwd=task["worktree"] on purpose (so evidence reflects the task branch), but this one silently diffs the main checkout's HEAD instead, which can call a graph fresh/stale incorrectly for any task whose worktree has diverged from ROOT.

The `graph` output field is documented as one of used|absent|stale|skipped, but only 'absent' (graph_links is None) and 'stale' (graph_fresh_for is not True) are given trigger conditions; 'skipped' has none, leaving it to implementer/test guesswork.

suggested_spec_changes: State explicitly that stale.py must wrap the injected git callable into the `git(cwd, *args)` shape before passing it into gitutil.moved_paths / gitutil.changed_paths, rather than reusing it as-is — name the adapter so a reviewer can check for it.

Require evidence()/load_links() to pass a git callable bound to cwd=task['worktree'] into interference.graph_fresh_for's `git` parameter, so freshness is computed against the task branch instead of ROOT's HEAD.

Give a concrete condition for graph='skipped' (e.g. graph_links/graph supplied and fresh, but no moved path falls in scope/changed so the interface check never runs) to disambiguate it from 'absent' and 'stale'.
